solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Aid for speaker in traffic jam, reportedly? (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the answer is how the phrase sounds when said

blocks.note: a traffic jam is a queue of autos (cars)

annotation.surface: A speaker stuck in traffic, wondering what could help.
annotation.walkthrough: An Autocue is the screen that scrolls a presenter's script; the traffic jam is the wordplay, not the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade name used generically for a teleprompter, the device that feeds a speaker their lines.

entries.clue: Concert gear is a bit wet without lid (3)

indicatorNotes.without lid: in a down entry the lid is the top letter, so the first letter comes off

blocks.note: the top letter D is removed

annotation.surface: Rain at an outdoor gig has left the equipment damp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lid' works because this is a down answer: the first letter sits on top.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for amplifier, the speaker unit every band plays through, so gear by example.

entries.clue: Pair set off for walk, wearily (7)

indicatorNotes.off: off means gone wrong, like milk, so the letters are no longer in order

annotation.surface: Two people set off on a long, tiring walk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as setting out on the walk; only 'off' is the instruction, and 'set' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb carries the weariness in itself: dragging along on foot, tired or reluctant.

entries.clue: Prisoner picked up silver for dance (5)

indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the chemical symbol for silver, turned upward by 'picked up'

annotation.surface: A convict pockets some silver in exchange for a dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like the prisoner picking up loot, but it only turns AG over.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin American line dance, one person holding the hips of the next; a dance by example.

entries.clue: Some stolen gin especially for motors (7)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters in the words that follow are taken

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the second into the start of the third

annotation.surface: Stolen gin turns out to be handy as fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: stol(EN GIN ES)pecially: the answer spans all three words, with GIN sitting whole in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a motor and an engine both turn fuel into movement.

entries.clue: Steal from European’s garment (4)

blocks.note: to take from someone by theft

annotation.surface: Someone lifting a European's coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as belonging to the European, but it stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the garment.
annotation.definitionFit: A long loose outer garment, such as a dressing gown or a judge's gown; a garment by example.

entries.clue: Was transported on duck for Wild West show (5)

blocks.note: travelled on a horse or as a passenger
a duck is a zero score in cricket, O; 'on' puts it after

annotation.surface: Someone riding a duck as a novelty act at a Wild West show.
annotation.walkthrough: A duck is a batter's score of nothing in cricket, hence the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: Cowboys' bronco-riding and roping contests, the display most associated with the American West.

entries.clue: Pause quickly for meal (9)

annotation.surface: A quick stop to grab something to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The word literally means breaking the overnight fast, so the parts fit the meal as well as the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The first meal of the day, so a meal by example.

entries.clue: Twist back of shoulder in country (6)

indicatorNotes.back of: the back of a word is its end, so its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: the letter is placed within the country

blocks.note: a European country, split after its second letter to take R

annotation.surface: Someone twists the back of their shoulder while abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an injury, and the answer is one, but 'back of shoulder' is only a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Twisting a joint so the ligaments are wrenched: the verb sense of twist, as in twisting an ankle.

entries.clue: After start of great advert, acquire device (6)

indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.After: the acquiring word follows what has come before

annotation.surface: Seeing a great advert and buying the thing it sells.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the acquire-word comes last, behind the other two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small ingenious device or tool.

entries.clue: Transform OK chap into a pirate (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Transform: transforming something changes its shape, so the letters are reshaped

annotation.surface: Turning an ordinary decent fellow into a pirate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Into' reads as a link, but its letters are needed in the fodder, so the definition is only 'a pirate'.
annotation.definitionFit: A pirate by example: the villain of J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan, with a hook for a hand.

entries.clue: Writer inside boat at first requires kitchen utensil (3,6)

indicatorNotes.inside: the writer is put within the boat
indicatorNotes.at first: at the start, so only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: a light paddled boat, opened before its last letter
first letter of the next word, 'requires'

annotation.surface: A writer on a boat trip needs something to open the tins.
annotation.walkthrough: CANO(PEN)E then R. 'At first' belongs with 'requires', whose R is taken, while 'requires' also links to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A kitchen utensil by example: the hand tool for opening tins, called a tin opener in Britain.

entries.clue: Trainee — they’re regularly entering pub (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter
indicatorNotes.entering: the letters go into the pub

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of they're
an old word for a pub, opened after its second letter

annotation.surface: Trainees filing into the pub after work.
annotation.walkthrough: IN(TER)N. Take the odd letters of THEYRE, ignoring the apostrophe.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trainee or junior working to gain experience.

entries.clue: Broken biro in a city in Africa (7)

indicatorNotes.Broken: something broken falls apart, and its letters are put back in a new order

annotation.surface: A pen broke while someone was in an African city.
annotation.walkthrough: A biro is a ballpoint pen. 'In a' reads as the start of the location, but its letters are part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An African city by example: the capital of Kenya.

entries.clue: Watch horror film — it has its ups and downs (6)

annotation.definition: it has its ups and downs
annotation.surface: Watching a horror film is an emotional rollercoaster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ups and downs' sounds like a figure of speech about the film, but it is meant literally.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a playground plank whose ends rise and fall in turn.

entries.clue: Wear out part of car (7)

blocks.note: to tire completely, or use up entirely
the pipe carrying fumes away from the engine

annotation.surface: Some car component has worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like it is asking for hidden letters, but here it just means a component.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb means to tire out or use up; the noun is the car's fume pipe, which draws the used gases out.

entries.clue: Photo of hairstyle is the final insult? (7,4)

blocks.note: a picture of the line where hair is divided, read whimsically
a last cutting remark made on leaving

annotation.surface: Having a photo taken of your haircut is the last straw.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: read literally as a shot (photo) of a parting (the line where hair divides).
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a cutting last remark made on the way out, the insult that ends the exchange.

entries.clue: Rule part of Tangiers from the south (5)

indicatorNotes.part of: only part of the word is used
indicatorNotes.from the south: in a down entry south is the bottom, so the letters read upward

blocks.note: the middle five letters of Tangiers, read upward

annotation.surface: Governing a district of Tangiers in the south.
annotation.walkthrough: Tangiers is a port in northern Morocco; 'from the south' sounds like geography but means read upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rule as a monarch does.

entries.clue: Shred part of a fireplace (5)

blocks.note: to rub food against a rough surface into small strips, as with cheese
the metal frame that holds the burning fuel

annotation.surface: Tearing up part of a fireplace.
annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses: a kitchen verb and a fireside noun.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb is shredding cheese or vegetables; the noun is the iron frame holding coals in a fireplace.

entries.clue: Shade one doing exercises (6)

indicatorNotes.exercises: exercising puts something through its paces, moving the letters about

annotation.surface: Someone working out in the shade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doing exercises' reads as one phrase, but 'exercises' is a verb acting on DOING.
annotation.definitionFit: A shade by example: the deep violet-blue between blue and violet in the rainbow.

entries.clue: Charm a fish, half-heartedly (6)

indicatorNotes.half-heartedly: the heart of the fish is a double letter; with half of it gone, one of the pair drops out

blocks.note: one of the two middle Ls goes

annotation.surface: Trying, without much effort, to charm a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a verb here but it is the noun: a lucky charm.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun sense of charm: a trinket worn to ward off harm.

entries.clue: Historical period initially eclipsing Roman age (3)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so the initial letter of each word

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the three words

annotation.surface: One historical period outshining the Roman age.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay describes itself too: the answer is an age.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a distinct span of history, like the Victorian one.

entries.clue: Relative’s piano missing final piece (4)

indicatorNotes.missing final piece: the word is missing its final piece, its last letter, as a jigsaw might lack its last piece

blocks.note: short for a large concert piano

annotation.surface: A relative's piano is missing one of its parts.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', not a possessive: the relative is the trimmed piano.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal word for a grandmother, a relative by example.

entries.clue: Cold drink is a deceit, unfortunately (4,3)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: things going badly for the letters leave them jumbled

annotation.surface: A drink promised cold turns out to be a disappointing trick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link word; the fodder is just 'a deceit'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cold drink by example: tea chilled and served over ice.
